subject: Unable to accept supplier portal invite — certificate/trust anchor error

Cc: support@escrowlane.com
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Problem accepting Redwood supplier portal invite

Hi Sofia / Ben,

We tried to accept the supplier portal invite you sent for EscrowLane this morning but hit a TLS/certificate error in our corporate browser (Enterprise Edge behind a security proxy). The UI shows: "Error: trust anchor for certification path not found" and the claim button is disabled. I attached a screenshot (invite-screenshot.png).

This is blocking our PO onboarding — we need a PO number to process payment to start work. Can you advise a workaround?

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Vendor Operations — EscrowLane Inc.
Alicia.Ramos@escrowlane.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0172
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@escrowlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Problem accepting Redwood supplier portal invite

Hi Alicia — sorry for the friction and thanks for the screenshot.

Quick triage steps while we investigate:
- Try an incognito window or a different browser (Chrome/Firefox) if possible (sometimes proxy certificates are only applied to managed browsers).
- If your security team performs TLS inspection, they may need to whitelist our invite host (portal.redwoodinference.com / coupa-us-east-1.redwood.com) or allow the invite URL to pass through.
- Can you also send any browser console error or the full curl output (we can provide a test URL) — that will help SRE.

I'll loop in Ben and Marissa to get infra involved. If it helps, we can reissue the invite as a one-time claim code or provide an alternate acceptance link that doesn't include embedded redirects. Would your team prefer a short call with our SRE to do a quick whitelist / cert fingerprint exchange?

Proposed times: today 2:00pm or tomorrow 9:00am PT.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Vendor Success Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@escrowlane.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@escrowlane.com
Date: 2026-08-04T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Problem accepting Redwood supplier portal invite

Thanks Sofia — I tried Chrome incognito and saw the same error. Our corporate proxy does TLS inspection and replaces cert chains with our internal CA. The error in the browser console is: "net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID — trust anchor for certification path not found". I've attached the screenshot you saw and a short export of the error from the console (attached as coupa-error-log.txt).

If you can provide the server certificate chain or a certificate thumbprint for the invite domain, I can pass that to our security team to whitelist. The invite needs to be accepted before our accounts payable team can tie it to the PO.

If you can reissue an invite without redirect chaining (or provide a manual claim code) that might also bypass our proxy rule. A call would help — Alicia (and our IT lead) can do 2pm PT today.

Alicia Ramos
Vendor Operations — EscrowLane Inc.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: EscrowLane invite TLS inspection issue (internal)

Looping internally to get infra/SRE assistance. Summary of triage so far: external vendor (EscrowLane) hits "trust anchor not found" when clicking our Coupa/Central-Portal invite link; they are behind TLS-inspecting corporate proxy. They attached screenshot and basic console error.

Action plan (proposed):
1) SRE to fetch the invite URL and capture the certificate chain (include full PEMs). Provide certificate thumbprint (SHA256) and subject CN to vendor for whitelist.
2) If chain includes a CDN or redirector host that our vendor proxy flags, create an alternate one-time claim flow: generate a numeric claim code and send a short invite email with the code (no redirect link).
3) Reissue invite that points directly to the portal host (avoid third-party redirector) for EscrowLane if possible.
4) If required, approve a documented temporary exception (security signoff) — Marissa can advise on exception language and approver.

I will open INC-2026-4387 with SRE and paste vendor logs. Marissa — can you review for exception approval and coordinate with Legal if we need to provide a signed statement of the host cert?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Platform Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@escrowlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Problem accepting Redwood supplier portal invite — next steps and temporary workaround

Hi Alicia — thank you for the patience. Quick update after SRE review: our invite URL resolves directly to portal.redwoodinference.com and the certificate chain is issued by DigiCert (we captured the full PEMs). For your security team, the server certificate SHA256 thumbprint is: 3F:8A:9C:...:B2 (I attached the exported chain as coupa-error-log.txt).

Workarounds we can do immediately:
- One-time numeric claim code: I created claim code ESC-7X92-RT (expires in 48 hours). You can paste that into the "Claim an account" form at https://portal.redwoodinference.com/manual-claim and skip the redirect flow.
- Reissued invite with direct portal link (no third-party redirector) has been sent in a separate email (subject: "Redwood supplier invite — direct link").

If your IT can accept the DigiCert chain/thumbprint or whitelist portal.redwoodinference.com, that will remove the friction long term. If they prefer, our SRE can join a 20-minute call to exchange the certificate and confirm the exact hostnames to whitelist — Ben, please confirm availability.

Please try the claim code and let me know whether the account is accepted; if it still fails we'll jump on the call.

Best,
— Sofia
